title: Strategy leaderboard — integration desk
ranking_basis: hard gates passed → graded sample size → MAE. Gates are pass/fail with no weighting, so a cosmetic lead cannot be bought with a soft score.
reward_policy: No entry is VALIDATED, therefore no reward is payable to any of them. This table is informational, and the honest headline is that the best model on this desk is not distinguishable from a naive pick.

rows.name: Originated margin + total (no absence term)
rows.metric: MAE in points against official FINAL scores, ratings fitted on an earlier window
rows.why: The only candidate on this desk whose inputs are all official, all point-in-time and all out-of-sample. It is not worse than a naive pick, and that is the whole claim.
rows.blocking_gates: V2 sample floor (n=51 < 100), V9 availability, V13 absence term ungraded
rows.what_moves_it_up: 100+ graded games and any closing-price file; nothing else can promote it.

rows.name: Same, with rest / home-court adjustments on
rows.metric: ΔMAE of each component, measured one at a time
rows.why: HCA is worth +0.05 MAE, back-to-back +0.01, shrinkage +0.36 — all inside a ±2.8 interval. The adjustments are kept because theory supports them, and flagged because this sample cannot confirm them.
rows.what_moves_it_up: A second and third graded week; the code path is unchanged meanwhile.

rows.name: Build B LBS leaderboard (S1–S8)
rows.why: Scored on 51 games with a 10/20–11/05 ratings window, so it is not look-ahead contaminated — but its Brier and log-loss both came out slightly worse than the reference, and its own conclusion was 'model ≈ market, within noise'.
rows.what_moves_it_up: Nothing inside the sandbox: it needs prices.

rows.name: Build A ledger (RecordLine-1 and its four families)
rows.metric: NOT VALIDATION. Look-ahead bias is present because the team stats cover the same games being predicted. Use this to confirm the pipeline runs, not to claim skill.
rows.why: Its own metadata labels the 14-game test CONTAMINATED — season-to-date inputs include the games being predicted. Read as a pipeline check only.
rows.what_moves_it_up: Re-fit on a DateFrom/DateTo window (now proven reachable) — that is exactly what INT-1 does.

rows.name: Player-prop lines from measured game-log dispersion
rows.metric: dispersion measured on 12 player-games across 3 players
rows.why: Build A blocked every prop row with 'no game-log variance'. That blocker is now partly lifted — a σ exists and is published with an interval — but 3 players cannot price a 22-game slate, so no prop pick is published.
rows.blocking_gates: V11 props coverage, V2, V10 price
rows.what_moves_it_up: Per-game logs for the players actually in the slate: one reachable page per player. This is the cheapest unblock on the list.

rows.name: Same-game parlay inside Fréchet bounds
rows.metric: joint probability published as bounds, never a point
rows.why: Correlation between two legs of one player's line is measured at r values whose intervals cross zero at n=4. Publishing a joint price off that would be inventing a number.
rows.what_moves_it_up: 30+ logged player-games per player before a single-point correlation is defensible.

registers_disagree.resolution: 51 is the count this session could verify as FINAL with a clean pre-window fit. Build A's 14 were look-ahead contaminated by its own admission; Build B's 23 is a per-strategy graded-bet count, not a game count, so the two are not the same unit and were never divided into each other.

values.integration: variance measured for 3 players, still not slate-wide

registers_disagree.resolution: Both statements are true of their own capture date. The blocker moved from 'no data at all' to 'data for 3 players'.

not_a_gate_but_relevant.settlement: 51 games graded, 31 cannot be settled yet
not_a_gate_but_relevant.warning: the record above is graded against the model's own number and is ~50% by construction; it is printed so nobody has to guess that it was hidden
